questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Bergen is in Norway, a crucial country in the green transition, I wanted to see in first person how Norwegians deal with their "Norwegian paradox".
I always loved the nature in Norway and always wanted to try moving here to live: I wanted to have a grasp of its culture.
Additionally, UiB is famous for its oceanography department, a field I'm deeply interested in. 
Lastly, they grant international students accommodation, which helps take off the most stressful part about moving abroad

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very easy, the university website is well-organized and the process to apply was very easy (even for the accommodation).
Everyone was also very quick at replying to emails, which is crucial when you don't understand something on the webpages

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't think I received much assistance, but it wasn't needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Extremely easy, you just send the application and they give you a cheap accommodation!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It's off campus, but the tram allows you to get to the university in 15 minutes, It's true that living here kinda keeps you in the international bubble, which is great, but also limits the interaction with Norwegians.
Remember then to apply for a shared flat with many people!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As an Erasmus student, you are given access to most of the courses just by applying for them on the "student web" webpage. You can always withdraw for exams and it's very easy also to enroll in different courses. One of the easiest processes I've encountered in my academic experience in three different universities!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Quick replies from the secretary and the detailed description of the courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just register for all the courses you might want to follow, start following them in the first week, and then withdraw from those you don't feel like taking. It's the easiest and most effective way!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
One course changed the professor in the middle of the course, which made the teaching a bit inconsistent and a bit hard to understand the structure of the exam.
Overall, though, I think the amount of workload was perfect for the amount of ECTS in all the courses.
Additionally, all the professors are always ready to help you in everything you ask them!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took an introductory course in oceanography, but it gave me all the info I think I'll need in my career; no previous knowledge is strictly required.
The MA course was at an MA level, you really need to have a good grasp of the mathematical tools you learn in the Bachelor's.
I also took a course addressed both to Master's and Bachelor's students. I have to say that being a Master's student helped me a lot: my experience was very valuable in that course and made it way easier in the various assignments.  But again, the course was accessible to Bachelor's students as well

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Way better. My experience at UCPH has been strange; I felt left alone for most of my studies. Here, the professor is very present and really makes you feel understood.
Also, the mandatory assignments during the semester made it easier to study for the exams in the end: I didn't really have important and valuable assignments during the semester at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MAT253 - Fluid Mechanics
GEOF236 - Chemical Oceanography
SDG207 - Energy Transition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SDG207. Great course, it is very well-managed and gives you a ton of info.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The food is really expensive here. Cooking at home is way more expensive than in Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables and fruits. But in general the groceries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate, but I know from other students that it was very easy to join them. A bit harder if you are here only for one semester. It's also kinda easy to find a student job

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym is very cheap, and there a lot of students organizations you can join

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on their interests, I really don't know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking, as much as you can. Find some friends to go with and you'll enjoy your stay in Norway so much!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Norwegians are always welcoming and the social rules are easy to apply.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student organizations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that they rely on planned events to socialize with each other

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their willingness to talk to international students! Everyone speaks English and they want to know from you a lot of stuff! Very easy to talk with Norwegians!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The vibes are similar to the Danish ones. Go hiking. Try to find a scoail flat

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I've already said

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The great feedback from professors and the bonds with A LOT of international students I made here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in some courses that required more study than my flatmates. It was kinda hard to keep pace with my studies while at the same time being social.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
